newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: GCC states to spend $50 billion to lift oil output.
newsitem.headline: GCC states to spend $50 billion to lift oil output.

text.p: Gulf Arab states are expected to spend about $50 billion by the year 2000 to boost their oil production capacity, a Bahraini minister said on Saturday.

"It is expected that Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states would spend about $50 billion by the year 2000 to increase their oil production capacity," Oil and Industry Minister Sheikh Isa bin Ali al-Khalifa said.
"This would offer more investment opportunities in the region for oil companies," Sheikh Isa told the opening session of an oil conference in Bahrain.
The GCC, an economic and political alliance, groups Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and Kuwait. The six oil-rich states sit on 40 percent of the world oil reserves.
Sheikh Isa said Bahrain was studying several oil and gas projects in 1997 and 1998 including a 26 million dinar ($69 million) gas pipeline to provide gas for a new power plant.
Around 320 firms from 16 countries are participating in an exhibition on the side of the conference.
